notes: Procedure is carried rather than summarized. The formation and test windows, the ranking rule, the attrition rule and the pooled-variance statistic all appear with their parameters, which is the difference between an output a reader can act on and one they can only cite.

Negative and null results are given the same standing as positive ones: no reversal at a one-year formation horizon, 5.4 per cent with t = 0.77 at twelve months, and an experiment on which the authors ran no statistical tests at all. A skewed output would have kept the 24.6 per cent and dropped these.

The corpus's internal disagreements survive into the output rather than being resolved: the small-firm reading against the market-capitalization finding, Shiller against Marsh and Merton, Reinganum against Basu and Graham. The paper does not settle these and neither does the output.

The dissertation dependency is visible. Three claims that carry much of the study's defense -- the bias-against-the-hypothesis argument, the portfolio characteristics, and the robustness to other residual types -- rest on an unpublished source not in this corpus, and the output says so twice.

One distribution problem rather than a loss: the caveat that the 36 monthly t-statistics do not represent independent evidence is in the research-design entry, while the January entry reports three of those t-statistics. A reader retrieving the January entry alone would over-read them.

The output states throughout that this is one study, one dataset and one independence group. For a corpus of a single 1985 paper whose findings were later both replicated and contested, that framing is what keeps the entries honest.
reasoning: All fifty-three units reached an assertion, so nothing is lost and the question is whether the output is skewed. I checked the three places it could be. The procedure survives in usable form -- the 85-month data requirement, the 16 nonoverlapping three-year windows, the top-and-bottom-35 ranking and the permanent-drop rebalancing rule are stated, not described, so a reader could rerun the study. The negative results survive: the one-year null, the insignificant 5.4 per cent at twelve months, and the absence of significance tests on the five-year experiment are assertions in their own right rather than hedges attached to positive claims. The proportions match the paper: the reversal, the January effect and the design carry the most weight, and the literature review is background at low priority. The one thing an output-only reader would get wrong is that the caveat about the monthly t-statistics not being independent sits in the design entry while the monthly t-statistics themselves sit in the January entry.
